summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive digital storytelling project that brings the forgotten history of NASA’s space missions back to life. We developed an e-magazine for school-aged children featuring stories of spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

Each story explores the purpose of the mission, the equipment’s scientific contributions, its journey, and what remains today. By combining historical information with engaging storytelling, our project addresses the challenge of documenting NASA’s abandoned space hardware and preserving its legacy.

We believe these objects are more than forgotten pieces of machinery; they are symbols of human curiosity, exploration, and scientific achievement. Our goal is to raise awareness of their importance, make space exploration history accessible to everyone, and remind people that even when a mission ends, its discoveries and contributions live on.
details: Our project teaches school-age children about the equipment and spacecraft sent into space for exploration, in a way that is easy to understand and engaging. It works as an interactive, story-based e-magazine that makes learning both educational and fun. This helps strengthen children’s knowledge of space, and because it is an e-magazine, it is easy for everyone to access. Our goal is to help children discover their interest in space at an early age, so that future space exploration can be carried forward by the people they grow up to become. To create it, we used NASA’s publicly available data for information, the AI tool Gemini to generate the visuals, and Canva for the design.
